sanskrit: tad uktam atikāyasya balino bāhuśālinaḥ kumbhakarṇasya vacanaṃ śrutvovāca mahodaraḥ
english: Having heard those words spoken by mighty Atikāya, the powerful, long-armed Kumbhakarṇa, Mahodara then replied.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇakule jāto dhṛṣṭaḥ prākṛtadarśanaḥ avalipto na śaknoṣi kṛtyaṃ sarvatra veditum
english: "Born in the clan of Kumbhakarṇa, you are insolent and of common understanding; filled with conceit, you are unable to discern what is proper in every matter.

sanskrit: na hi rājā na jānīte kumbhakarṇa nayānayau tvaṃ tu kaiśorakād dhṛṣṭaḥ kevalaṃ vaktum icchasi
english: The king surely knows what is sound policy and what is not, O Kumbhakarṇa; but you, insolent since boyhood, desire only to bluster.

sanskrit: sthānaṃ vṛddhiṃ ca hāniṃ ca deśakālavibhāgavit ātmanaś ca pareṣāṃ ca budhyate rākṣasarṣabha
english: One who understands the division of place and time discerns what is stable, what is growth, and what is decline — both for himself and for others, O bull among rākṣasas.

sanskrit: yat tu śakyaṃ balavatā kartuṃ prākṛtabuddhinā anupāsitavṛddhena kaḥ kuryāt tādṛśaṃ budhaḥ
english: What a mighty one of ordinary intellect, who has not attended upon the wise elders, might do — what wise man would do likewise?

sanskrit: yāṃs tu dharmārthakāmāṃs tvaṃ bravīṣi pṛthag āśrayān anuboddhuṃ svabhāvena na hi lakṣaṇam asti te
english: As for the three — dharma, artha, and kāma — which you expound as separate pursuits to be understood: by your very nature you show no sign of comprehending them.

sanskrit: karma caiva hi sarveṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ prayojanam śreyaḥ pāpīyasāṃ cātra phalaṃ bhavati karmaṇām
english: For action is the purpose of all causes; and here the fruit of actions falls out as either good or evil.

sanskrit: niḥśreyasa phalāv eva dharmārthāv itarāv api adharmānarthayoḥ prāptiḥ phalaṃ ca pratyavāyikam
english: Dharma and artha both yield the fruit of the highest good; the opposite pair — adharma and anartha — bear only harmful fruit.

sanskrit: aihalaukikapāratryaṃ karma pumbhir niṣevyate karmāṇy api tu kalpyāni labhate kāmam āsthitaḥ
english: Men perform action for this world and the next; and by fixing upon the ordained actions, one also attains kāma.

sanskrit: tatra kḷptam idaṃ rājñā hṛdi kāryaṃ mataṃ ca naḥ śatrau hi sāhasaṃ yat syāt kim ivātrāpanīyate
english: In that regard, what the king has determined in his heart is deemed proper by us; for if there is rashness toward the enemy, what harm could be removed from it?

sanskrit: ekasyaivābhiyāne tu hetur yaḥ prakṛtas tvayā tatrāpy anupapannaṃ te vakṣyāmi yad asādhu ca
english: As for the reasoning you have advanced for going alone against the enemy — even in that I will tell you what is improper and what is not sound.

sanskrit: yena pūrvaṃ janasthāne bahavo 'tibalā hatāḥ rākṣasā rāghavaṃ taṃ tvaṃ katham eko jayiṣyasi
english: He by whom many exceedingly mighty rākṣasas were slain formerly at Janasthāna — how will you alone conquer that Rāghava?

sanskrit: ye purā nirjitās tena janasthāne mahaujasā rākṣasāṃs tān pure sarvān bhītān adyāpi paśyasi
english: Those great-spirited rākṣasas who were defeated by him at Janasthāna — even today you see them all in the city, still in fear.

sanskrit: taṃ siṃham iva saṃkruddhaṃ rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam sarpaṃ suptam ivābuddhyā prabodhayitum icchasi
english: That Rāma, son of Daśaratha, who is like an enraged lion — you wish, like one who unknowingly stirs a sleeping serpent, to rouse him.

sanskrit: jvalantaṃ tejasā nityaṃ krodhena ca durāsadam kas taṃ mṛtyum ivāsahyam āsādayitum arhati
english: Who is fit to approach him who always blazes with splendour and is unapproachable in wrath — approaching him is like approaching unbearable Death?

sanskrit: saṃśayastham idaṃ sarvaṃ śatroḥ pratisamāsane ekasya gamanaṃ tatra na hi me rocate tava
english: All of this is fraught with doubt in confronting that enemy; your going there alone does not at all please me.

sanskrit: hīnārthas tu samṛddhārthaṃ ko ripuṃ prākṛto yathā niścitaṃ jīvitatyāge vaśam ānetum icchati
english: Who, like a common man of diminished resources, would seek to bring under control a powerful enemy clearly at the cost of his own life?

sanskrit: yasya nāsti manuṣyeṣu sadṛśo rākṣasottama katham āśaṃsase yoddhuṃ tulyenendravivasvatoḥ
english: He who has no equal among men, O foremost of rākṣasas — how do you hope to fight one who is the peer of Indra and Vivasvat?

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu saṃrabdhaṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahodaraḥ uvāca rakṣasāṃ madhye rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇam
english: Having thus addressed the enraged Kumbhakarṇa, Mahodara then spoke in the midst of the rākṣasas to Rāvaṇa, who makes the worlds cry out.

sanskrit: labdhvā punas tāṃ vaidehīṃ kimarthaṃ tvaṃ prajalpasi yadecchasi tadā sītā vaśagā te bhaviṣyati
english: "Having regained Vaidehī, why do you babble on? When you desire it, Sītā will be in your power.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭaḥ kaś cid upāyo me sītopasthānakārakaḥ rucitaś cet svayā buddhyā rākṣaseśvara taṃ śṛṇu
english: A certain stratagem has occurred to me for bringing Sītā to compliance; if it pleases you, lord of rākṣasas, hear it.

sanskrit: ahaṃ dvijihvaḥ saṃhrādī kumbhakarṇo vitardanaḥ pañcarāmavadhāyaete niryāntīty avaghoṣaya
english: Have it proclaimed: 'I — Dvijihva — and Saṃhrādī, Kumbhakarṇa, and Vitardana go forth now to slay Rāma.'

sanskrit: tato gatvā vayaṃ yuddhaṃ dāsyāmas tasya yatnataḥ jeṣyāmo yadi te śatrūn nopāyaiḥ kṛtyam asti naḥ
english: Then, going forth, we shall give him battle with full effort; if we conquer your enemies, stratagem is unnecessary for us.

sanskrit: atha jīvati naḥ śatrur vayaṃ ca kṛtasaṃyugāḥ tataḥ samabhipatsyāmo manasā yat samīkṣitum
english: But if the enemy survives and we have engaged in battle, then we shall execute what has been deliberated in the mind.

sanskrit: vayaṃ yuddhād ihaiṣyāmo rudhireṇa samukṣitāḥ vidārya svatanuṃ bāṇai rāmanāmāṅkitaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: We shall return here from the battle drenched in blood, our own bodies pierced by the sharp arrows bearing the name of Rāma.

sanskrit: bhakṣito rāghavo 'smābhir lakṣmaṇaś ceti vādinaḥ tava pādau grahīṣyāmas tvaṃ naḥ kāma prapūraya
english: Declaring 'We have devoured Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa,' we shall grasp your feet; you, fulfil our desire.

sanskrit: tato 'vaghoṣaya pure gajaskandhena pārthiva hato rāmaḥ saha bhrātrā sasainya iti sarvataḥ
english: Then proclaim throughout the city from the back of an elephant, O king: 'Rāma has been slain along with his brother and his army.'

sanskrit: prīto nāma tato bhūtvā bhṛtyānāṃ tvam ariṃdama bhogāṃś ca parivārāṃś ca kāmāṃś ca vasudāpaya
english: Then, O subduer of foes, becoming indeed pleased with your servants, bestow upon them enjoyments, retinues, and desires.

sanskrit: tato mālyāni vāsāṃsi vīrāṇām anulepanam peyaṃ ca bahu yodhebhyaḥ svayaṃ ca muditaḥ piba
english: Then give garlands, garments, and ointments to the heroes; give abundant drink to the warriors, and yourself drink in joy.

sanskrit: tato 'smin bahulībhūte kaulīne sarvato gate praviśyāśvāsya cāpi tvaṃ sītāṃ rahasi sāntvaya dhanadhānyaiś ca kāmaiś ca ratnaiś caināṃ pralobhaya
english: Then, when this merriment has multiplied and spread everywhere, entering in private, reassure and soothe Sītā, and entice her with wealth, grain, pleasures, and jewels.

sanskrit: anayopadhayā rājan bhayaśokānubandhayā akāmā tvadvaśaṃ sītā naṣṭanāthā gamiṣyati
english: By this ruse, O king — bound to fear and grief — Sītā, bereft of her lord and unwilling, will come under your sway.

sanskrit: rañjanīyaṃ hi bhartāraṃ vinaṣṭam avagamya sā nairāśyāt strīlaghutvāc ca tvadvaśaṃ pratipatsyate
english: Learning that her worthy husband is destroyed, she, out of despair and the lightness of a woman's nature, will submit to your will.

sanskrit: sā purā sukhasaṃvṛddhā sukhārhā duḥkhakarṣitā tvayy adhīnaḥ sukhaṃ jñātvā sarvathopagamiṣyati
english: She who was formerly reared in happiness and worthy of happiness, now tormented by misery — knowing that happiness depends on you — will in every way come to you.

sanskrit: etat sunītaṃ mama darśanena rāmaṃ hi dṛṣṭvaiva bhaved anarthaḥ ihaiva te setsyati motsuko bhūr mahān ayuddhena sukhasya lābhaḥ
english: This, in my view, is sound policy; for upon merely seeing Rāma, disaster would befall. Here your great longing shall be fulfilled — gain of happiness without battle.

sanskrit: anaṣṭasainyo hy anavāptasaṃśayo ripūn ayuddhena jayañ janādhipa yaśaś ca puṇyaṃ ca mahan mahīpate śriyaṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca ciraṃ samaśnute
english: A lord of men who, without losing his army and without encountering doubt, conquers his enemies without battle, O master of the earth, long enjoys great glory, merit, prosperity, and fame."

sanskrit: sa tathoktas tu nirbhartsya kumbhakarṇo mahodaram abravīd rākṣasaśreṣṭhaṃ bhrātaraṃ rāvaṇaṃ tataḥ
english: Thus spoken to, Kumbhakarṇa rebuked Mahodara, then addressed his brother Rāvaṇa, foremost among rākṣasas.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tava bhayaṃ ghoraṃ vadhāt tasya durātmanaḥ rāmasyādya pramārjāmi nirvairas tvaṃ sukhībhava
english: "I shall this day wipe away your terrible fear of death at the hands of that wicked Rāma; be free from enmity and dwell in happiness.

sanskrit: garjanti na vṛthā śūra nirjalā iva toyadāḥ paśya saṃpādyamānaṃ tu garjitaṃ yudhi karmaṇā
english: Heroes do not roar in vain, as waterless clouds do; see now my roar being fulfilled in battle by deed.

sanskrit: na marṣayati cātmānaṃ saṃbhāvayati nātmanā adarśayitvā śūrās tu karma kurvanti duṣkaram
english: Heroes neither endure passively nor glorify themselves; without showing off, they perform deeds of great difficulty.

sanskrit: viklavānām abuddhīnāṃ rājñāṃ paṇḍitamāninām śṛṇvatām ādita idaṃ tvadvidhānāṃ mahodara
english: This is what first befalls kings who are confused, devoid of wisdom, and fancying themselves learned — those who listen to the likes of you, Mahodara.

sanskrit: yuddhe kāpuruṣair nityaṃ bhavadbhiḥ priyavādibhiḥ rājānam anugacchadbhiḥ kṛtyam etad vināśitam
english: This matter has been ruined by cowards like you, ever speaking pleasant words, following the king about in battle.

sanskrit: rājaśeṣā kṛtā laṅkā kṣīṇaḥ kośo balaṃ hatam rājānam imam āsādya suhṛccihnam amitrakam
english: Laṅkā has been reduced to but the shadow of a kingdom; the treasury is exhausted, the army slaughtered — all through attending upon this king who wears the mark of a friend but is an enemy.

sanskrit: eṣa niryāmy ahaṃ yuddham udyataḥ śatrunirjaye durnayaṃ bhavatām adya samīkartuṃ mahāhave
english: I now march forth for battle, intent on conquering the enemy, to rectify today in the great conflict the ill counsel of yourselves.

sanskrit: evam uktavato vākyaṃ kumbhakarṇasya dhīmataḥ pratyuvāca tato vākyaṃ prahasan rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Having heard these words of the wise Kumbhakarṇa, the lord of rākṣasas then replied, laughing.

sanskrit: mahodaro 'yaṃ rāmāt tu paritrasto na saṃśayaḥ na hi rocayate tāta yuddhaṃ yuddhaviśārada
english: "This Mahodara is certainly terrified of Rāma — no doubt; he does not relish battle, dear one, though expert in warfare.

sanskrit: kaś cin me tvatsamo nāsti sauhṛdena balena ca gaccha śatruvadhāya tvaṃ kumbhakarṇajayāya ca
english: There is no one equal to you for me in affection and in strength; go for the slaying of the enemy and for the triumph of Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: ādade niśitaṃ śūlaṃ vegāc chatrunibarhaṇaḥ sarvakālāyasaṃ dīptaṃ taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇam
english: The swift annihilator of enemies then took up the sharp spear — made entirely of iron, blazing, and adorned with beaten gold —

sanskrit: indrāśanisamaṃ bhīmaṃ vajrapratimagauravam devadānavagandharvayakṣakiṃnarasūdanam
english: fearsome as Indra's thunderbolt, equal in weight to the vajra, the slayer of gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, and kiṃnaras —

sanskrit: raktamālya mahādāma svataś codgatapāvakam ādāya niśitaṃ śūlaṃ śatruśoṇitarañjitam kumbhakarṇo mahātejā rāvaṇaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: garlanded with red wreaths of great length, shooting forth flames of itself, stained with the blood of enemies. Taking up that sharp spear, the greatly resplendent Kumbhakarṇa spoke to Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: gamiṣyāmy aham ekākī tiṣṭhatv iha balaṃ mahat adya tān kṣudhitaḥ kruddho bhakṣayiṣyāmi vānarān
english: "I shall go alone; let the great army remain here. Today, hungry and wrathful, I shall devour those monkeys.

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇavacaḥ śrutvā rāvaṇo vākyam abravīt sainyaiḥ parivṛto gaccha śūlamudgalapāṇibhiḥ
english: Hearing Kumbhakarṇa's words, Rāvaṇa replied: "Go surrounded by troops bearing spears and clubs in their hands.

sanskrit: vānarā hi mahātmānaḥ śīghrāś ca vyavasāyinaḥ ekākinaṃ pramattaṃ vā nayeyur daśanaiḥ kṣayam
english: For the monkeys are noble-souled, swift, and resolute; they could bring even one alone or careless to destruction with their teeth.

sanskrit: tasmāt paramadurdharṣaiḥ sainyaiḥ parivṛto vraja rakṣasām ahitaṃ sarvaṃ śatrupakṣaṃ nisūdaya
english: Therefore go surrounded by utterly irresistible troops; annihilate the entire enemy host, which is hostile to the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: athāsanāt samutpatya srajaṃ maṇikṛtāntarām ābabandha mahātejāḥ kumbhakarṇasya rāvaṇaḥ
english: Then, springing up from his seat, the greatly resplendent Rāvaṇa bound upon Kumbhakarṇa a garland set with jewels at intervals.

sanskrit: aṅgadān aṅgulīveṣṭān varāṇy ābharaṇāni ca hāraṃ ca śaśisaṃkāśam ābabandha mahātmanaḥ
english: He fastened armlets, finger-rings, and choice ornaments upon the great-souled one, as well as a necklace bright as the moon.

sanskrit: divyāni ca sugandhīni mālyadāmāni rāvaṇaḥ śrotre cāsajjayām āsa śrīmatī cāsya kuṇḍale
english: Rāvaṇa also attached divine, fragrant garland-chains, and fastened upon his ears his resplendent earrings.

sanskrit: kāñcanāṅgadakeyūro niṣkābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ kumbhakarṇo bṛhatkarṇaḥ suhuto 'gnir ivābabhau
english: Adorned with golden armlets and upper-arm bands, decorated with necklace-ornaments, large-eared Kumbhakarṇa blazed like a well-fed fire.

sanskrit: śroṇīsūtreṇa mahatā mecakena virājitaḥ amṛtotpādane naddho bhujaṃgeneva mandaraḥ
english: Resplendent with a great dark waist-cord, he shone like Mount Mandara when it was bound with the serpent at the churning of the nectar.

sanskrit: sa kāñcanaṃ bhārasahaṃ nivātaṃ vidyutprabhaṃ dīptam ivātmabhāsā ābadhyamānaḥ kavacaṃ rarāja saṃdhyābhrasaṃvīta ivādrirājaḥ
english: As the golden armour — capable of bearing great weight, windproof, bright as lightning, blazing with its own radiance — was being fastened upon him, he shone like the king of mountains wrapped in twilight clouds.

sanskrit: sarvābharaṇanaddhāṅgaḥ śūlapāṇiḥ sa rākṣasaḥ trivikramakṛtotsāho nārāyaṇa ivābabhau
english: His body bound with every ornament, spear in hand, that rākṣasa, his valour akin to that of the three-striding one, appeared like Nārāyaṇa himself.

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ saṃpariṣvajya kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam praṇamya śirasā tasmai saṃpratasthe mahābaliḥ tam āśīrbhiḥ praśastābhiḥ preṣayām āsa rāvaṇaḥ
english: Embracing his brother, circling him clockwise, and bowing his head to him, the mighty one set forth; and Rāvaṇa sent him off with auspicious benedictions.

sanskrit: śaṅkhadundubhinirghoṣaiḥ sainyaiś cāpi varāyudhaiḥ taṃ gajaiś ca turaṃgaiś ca syandanaiś cāmbudasvanaiḥ anujagmur mahātmānaṃ rathino rathināṃ varam
english: With the blare of conches and kettledrums, and with troops bearing choice weapons, with elephants, horses, and chariots thundering like rain-clouds, chariot-warriors followed that great-souled one, the foremost of chariot-fighters.

sanskrit: sarpair uṣṭraiḥ kharair aśvaiḥ siṃhadvipamṛgadvijaiḥ anujagmuś ca taṃ ghoraṃ kumbhakarṇaṃ mahābalam
english: With serpents, camels, donkeys, horses, lions, elephants, deer, and birds, they followed that terrible and mighty Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: sa puṣpavarṇair avakīryamāṇo dhṛtātapatraḥ śitaśūlapāṇiḥ madotkaṭaḥ śoṇitagandhamatto viniryayau dānavadevaśatruḥ
english: Showered with flowers of varied colours, holding an umbrella aloft, sharp spear in hand, intoxicated with frenzy, maddened by the scent of blood, the foe of dānavas and gods marched forth.

sanskrit: padātayaś ca bahavo mahānādā mahābalāḥ anvayū rākṣasā bhīmā bhīmākṣāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ
english: Many foot-soldiers followed him — fearsome rākṣasas of great strength and terrible eyes, roaring loudly, weapons in hand.

sanskrit: raktākṣāḥ sumahākāyā nīlāñjanacayopamāḥ śūrān udyamya khaḍgāṃś ca niśitāṃś ca paraśvadhān
english: Red-eyed, of immense bodies, resembling mounds of blue collyrium, brandishing sharp swords and axes —

sanskrit: bahuvyāmāṃś ca vipulān kṣepaṇīyān durāsadān tālaskandhāṃś ca vipulān kṣepaṇīyān durāsadān
english: and great missiles many fathoms long, vast and irresistible, and broad palm-tree trunks as well, vast and unapproachable —

sanskrit: athānyad vapur ādāya dāruṇaṃ lomaharṣaṇam niṣpapāta mahātejāḥ kumbhakarṇo mahābalaḥ
english: Then, assuming another terrible form that made the hair stand on end, the greatly resplendent and mighty Kumbhakarṇa burst forth.

sanskrit: dhanuḥśataparīṇāhaḥ sa ṣaṭśatasamucchitaḥ raudraḥ śakaṭacakrākṣo mahāparvatasaṃnibhaḥ
english: His girth measured a hundred bow-lengths around; he rose to six hundred bow-lengths in height — a fearsome one, his eyes like chariot-wheels, resembling a great mountain.

sanskrit: saṃnipatya ca rakṣāṃsi dagdhaśailopamo mahān kumbhakarṇo mahāvaktraḥ prahasann idam abravīt
english: Joining the rākṣasas, the great one resembling a scorched mountain, wide-mouthed Kumbhakarṇa, laughing, spoke thus:

sanskrit: adya vānaramukhyānāṃ tāni yūthāni bhāgaśaḥ nirdahiṣyāmi saṃkruddhaḥ śalabhān iva pāvakaḥ
english: "Today, enraged, I shall burn those hosts of monkey-chiefs troop by troop, as fire burns locusts.

sanskrit: nāparādhyanti me kāmaṃ vānarā vanacāriṇaḥ jātir asmadvidhānāṃ sā purodyānavibhūṣaṇam
english: The forest-roaming monkeys have done me no real wrong; creatures like them are the natural ornament of parks and gardens.

sanskrit: purarodhasya mūlaṃ tu rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ hate tasmin hataṃ sarvaṃ taṃ vadhiṣyāmi saṃyuge
english: But the root of the siege of the city is Rāghava together with Lakṣmaṇa; when he is slain, all is slain — him I shall kill in battle."

sanskrit: evaṃ tasya bruvāṇasya kumbhakarṇasya rākṣasāḥ nādaṃ cakrur mahāghoraṃ kampayanta ivārṇavam
english: As Kumbhakarṇa spoke thus, the rākṣasas set up a mighty and terrible roar, as if shaking the ocean.

sanskrit: tasya niṣpatatas tūrṇaṃ kumbhakarṇasya dhīmataḥ babhūvur ghorarūpāṇi nimittāni samantataḥ
english: As the wise Kumbhakarṇa swiftly burst forth, terrible omens appeared on all sides.

sanskrit: ulkāśaniyutā meghā vineduś ca sudāruṇāḥ sasāgaravanā caiva vasudhā samakampata
english: Clouds mixed with meteors and thunderbolts rumbled most dreadfully; the earth with its oceans and forests trembled.

sanskrit: ghorarūpāḥ śivā neduḥ sajvālakavalair mukhaiḥ maṇḍalāny apasavyāni babandhuś ca vihaṃgamāḥ
english: Jackals of fearsome aspect howled with flaming morsels in their mouths; birds wheeled in inauspicious circles.

sanskrit: niṣpapāta ca gṛdhre 'sya śūle vai pathi gacchataḥ prāsphuran nayanaṃ cāsya savyo bāhur akampata
english: A vulture alighted upon his spear as he walked the road; his eye throbbed and his left arm trembled.

sanskrit: niṣpapāta tadā coklā jvalantī bhīmanisvanā ādityo niṣprabhaś cāsīn na pravāti sukho 'nilaḥ
english: A blazing meteor fell then with a fearsome sound; the sun lost its lustre, and no pleasant breeze blew.

sanskrit: acintayan mahotpātān utthitāṃl lomaharṣaṇān niryayau kumbhakarṇas tu kṛtāntabalacoditaḥ
english: Heeding not the great and hair-raising portents that had arisen, Kumbhakarṇa marched out, impelled by the force of Death.

sanskrit: sa laṅghayitvā prākāraṃ padbhyāṃ parvatasaṃnibhaḥ dadarśābhraghanaprakhyaṃ vānarānīkam adbhutam
english: Stepping over the rampart on foot, mountain-like, he beheld the wondrous monkey-army, dense as a mass of clouds.

sanskrit: te dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaśreṣṭhaṃ vānarāḥ parvatopamam vāyununnā iva ghanā yayuḥ sarvā diśas tadā
english: Seeing that foremost rākṣasa who was like a mountain, the monkeys fled in all directions then, like storm-driven clouds.

sanskrit: tad vānarānīkam atipracaṇḍaṃ diśo dravad bhinnam ivābhrajālam sa kumbhakarṇaḥ samavekṣya harṣān nanāda bhūyo ghanavad ghanābhaḥ
english: Seeing that exceedingly fierce monkey-army scatter in all directions like a broken mass of clouds, Kumbhakarṇa, who resembled a cloud, roared again in joy, like a thunder-cloud.

sanskrit: te tasya ghoraṃ ninadaṃ niśamya yathā ninādaṃ divi vāridasya petur dharaṇyāṃ bahavaḥ plavaṃgā nikṛttamūlā iva sālavṛkṣāḥ
english: Hearing his terrible roar, as though it were the rumble of a cloud in the sky, many leaping monkeys fell to the ground, like sāla-trees with their roots cut.

sanskrit: vipulaparighavān sa kumbhakarṇo ripunidhanāya viniḥsṛto mahātmā kapi gaṇabhayam ādadat subhīmaṃ prabhur iva kiṃkaradaṇḍavān yugānte
english: That great-souled Kumbhakarṇa, bearing his broad iron club, having gone forth to slay the enemy, struck profound terror into the monkey-hosts, like a master wielding his rod of punishment at the world's end.

sanskrit: sa nanāda mahānādaṃ samudram abhinādayan janayann iva nirghātān vidhamann iva parvatān
english: He roared a mighty roar, resounding over the ocean, as if generating thunderclaps, as if shattering mountains.

sanskrit: tam avadhyaṃ maghavatā yamena varuṇena ca prekṣya bhīmākṣam āyāntaṃ vānarā vipradudruvuḥ
english: Seeing him approach with his terrible eyes — he who was invincible by Indra, Yama, or Varuṇa — the monkeys fled in all directions.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu vidravato dṛṣṭvā vāliputro 'ṅgado 'bravīt nalaṃ nīlaṃ gavākṣaṃ ca kumudaṃ ca mahābalam
english: Seeing them running away, Aṅgada, son of Vālin, addressed Nala, Nīla, Gavākṣa, and the mighty Kumuda:

sanskrit: ātmānam atra vismṛtya vīryāṇy abhijanāni ca kva gacchata bhayatrastāḥ prākṛtā harayo yathā
english: "Forgetting yourselves here — your valour and your noble birth — where do you go, panicked with fear, like common monkeys?

sanskrit: sādhu saumyā nivartadhvaṃ kiṃ prāṇān parirakṣatha nālaṃ yuddhāya vai rakṣo mahatīyaṃ vibhīṣikāḥ
english: Turn back, gentle ones; why do you protect your lives? This rākṣasa is not fit for battle — this great menace is mere terror.

sanskrit: mahatīm utthitām enāṃ rākṣasānāṃ vibhīṣikām vikramād vidhamiṣyāmo nivartadhvaṃ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: This great terror of the rākṣasas that has arisen — we shall scatter it by our valour; turn back, O leaping ones."

sanskrit: kṛcchreṇa tu samāśvāsya saṃgamya ca tatas tataḥ vṛkṣādrihastā harayaḥ saṃpratasthū raṇājiram
english: With great difficulty reassuring them and rallying them from here and there, the monkeys, with trees and boulders in hand, set forth toward the battle-field.

sanskrit: te nivṛtya tu saṃkruddhāḥ kumbhakarṇaṃ vanaukasaḥ nijaghnuḥ paramakruddhāḥ samadā iva kuñjarāḥ prāṃśubhir giriśṛṅgaiś ca śilābhiś ca mahābalāḥ
english: Turning back, those forest-dwellers, exceedingly enraged, struck Kumbhakarṇa — like rut-maddened elephants — hurling tall mountain-peaks and boulders, the mighty ones.

sanskrit: pādapaiḥ puṣpitāgraiś ca hanyamāno na kampate tasya gātreṣu patitā bhidyante śataśaḥ śilāḥ pādapāḥ puṣpitāgrāś ca bhagnāḥ petur mahītale
english: Though struck with flowering-topped trees, he did not tremble; the boulders that fell upon his limbs shattered into hundreds of pieces, and the flowering-topped trees broke and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: so 'pi sainyāni saṃkruddho vānarāṇāṃ mahaujasām mamantha paramāyatto vanāny agnir ivotthitaḥ
english: He too, enraged, with utmost effort, ground down the armies of the mighty monkeys, like a blazing fire consuming forests.

sanskrit: lohitārdrās tu bahavaḥ śerate vānararṣabhāḥ nirastāḥ patitā bhūmau tāmrapuṣpā iva drumāḥ
english: Many foremost monkeys, drenched in blood, lay prostrate — cast down and fallen upon the earth like trees with copper-red blossoms.

sanskrit: laṅghayantaḥ pradhāvanto vānarā nāvalokayan ke cit samudre patitāḥ ke cid gaganam āśritāḥ
english: The monkeys, leaping and running, looked not back; some fell into the ocean, some took refuge in the sky.

sanskrit: vadhyamānās tu te vīrā rākṣasena balīyasā sāgaraṃ yena te tīrṇāḥ pathā tenaiva dudruvuḥ
english: Those heroes, being slaughtered by the mighty rākṣasa, fled by the very path by which they had crossed the ocean.

sanskrit: te sthalāni tathā nimnaṃ viṣaṇṇavadanā bhayāt ṛkṣā vṛkṣān samārūḍhāḥ ke cit parvatam āśritāḥ
english: With dejected faces, in fear, the bears and monkeys took to open ground and valleys; some climbed into trees, some took refuge on a mountain.

sanskrit: mamajjur arṇave ke cid guhāḥ ke cit samāśritāḥ niṣeduḥ plavagāḥ ke cit ke cin naivāvatasthire
english: Some plunged into the sea, some took shelter in caves; some monkeys sat still, some did not stand their ground at all.

sanskrit: tān samīkṣyāṅgado bhaṅgān vānarān idam abravīt avatiṣṭhata yudhyāmo nivartadhvaṃ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: Seeing those monkeys routed, Aṅgada spoke to them: "Stand firm; let us fight; turn back, O leaping ones.

sanskrit: bhagnānāṃ vo na paśyāmi parigamya mahīm imām sthānaṃ sarve nivartadhvaṃ kiṃ prāṇān parirakṣatha
english: Searching this entire earth, I see no refuge for you who are routed; all of you, turn back — why do you protect your lives?

sanskrit: nirāyudhānāṃ dravatām asaṃgagatipauruṣāḥ dārā hy apahasiṣyanti sa vai ghātas tu jīvitām
english: For those who run unarmed with unsupported flight and no valour — their own wives shall mock them; that truly is a blow against life.

sanskrit: kuleṣu jātāḥ sarve sma vistīrṇeṣu mahatsu ca anāryāḥ khalu yad bhītās tyaktvā vīryaṃ pradhāvata
english: We are all born in great and illustrious clans; it is surely ignoble that, in fear, abandoning your valour, you run away.

sanskrit: vikatthanāni vo yāni yadā vai janasaṃsadi tāni vaḥ kva ca yatāni sodagrāṇi mahānti ca
english: Those boasts of yours in the assembly of the people — where are they now? Where have those great and exalted resolves gone?

sanskrit: bhīrupravādāḥ śrūyante yas tu jīvati dhikkṛtaḥ mārgaḥ satpuruṣair juṣṭaḥ sevyatāṃ tyajyatāṃ bhayam
english: The taunts of 'coward' are heard — he who lives disgraced is cursed; follow the path trodden by men of honour; abandon fear.

sanskrit: śayāmahe vā nihatāḥ pṛthivyām alpajīvitāḥ duṣprāpaṃ brahmalokaṃ vā prāpnumo yudhi sūditāḥ saṃprāpnuyāmaḥ kīrtiṃ vā nihatya śatrum āhave
english: Let us lie slain upon the earth — we who have short lives — or, cut down in battle, attain the world of Brahmā, hard to reach; or let us gain glory by slaying the enemy in combat.

sanskrit: na kumbhakarṇaḥ kākutsthaṃ dṛṣṭvā jīvan gamiṣyati dīpyamānam ivāsādya pataṃgo jvalanaṃ yathā
english: Kumbhakarṇa, having seen Kākutstha, shall not go away living — like a moth approaching a blazing fire.

sanskrit: palāyanena coddiṣṭāḥ prāṇān rakṣāmahe vayam ekena bahavo bhagnā yaśo nāśaṃ gamiṣyati
english: We who were pointed at for fleeing — shall we protect our lives? Many routed by one — our glory shall come to nothing."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ taṃ śūram aṅgadaṃ kanakāṅgadam dravamāṇās tato vākyam ūcuḥ śūravigarhitam
english: As heroic Aṅgada of the golden armlets spoke thus, those still fleeing uttered words censured by the brave:

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ naḥ kadanaṃ ghoraṃ kumbhakarṇena rakṣasā na sthānakālo gacchāmo dayitaṃ jīvitaṃ hi naḥ
english: "Terrible carnage has been wrought upon us by the rākṣasa Kumbhakarṇa; this is no time to stand — we go; life is dear to us."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ sarve te bhejire diśaḥ bhīmaṃ bhīmākṣam āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānarayūthapāḥ
english: Having spoken only this much, all those monkey-troop leaders fled in all directions, seeing the fearsome, terrible-eyed one approaching.

sanskrit: dravamāṇās tu te vīrā aṅgadena valīmukhāḥ sāntvaiś ca bahumānaiś ca tataḥ sarve nivartitāḥ
english: But those fleeing heroes, the broad-faced monkeys, were then all turned back by Aṅgada with gentle words and great respect.

sanskrit: ṛṣabhaśarabhamaindadhūmranīlāḥ kumudasuṣeṇagavākṣarambhatārāḥ dvividapanasavāyuputramukhyās tvaritatarābhimukhaṃ raṇaṃ prayātāḥ
english: Ṛṣabha, Śarabha, Mainda, Dhūmra, and Nīla; Kumuda, Suṣeṇa, Gavākṣa, Rambha, and Tāra; Dvivida, Panasa, and Vāyuputra as chief — all set out swiftly toward the battle.
